reference: GNU coreutils sleep from the runner's /usr PATH for parity cases. The elapsed-time fixture measures with Bash EPOCHREALTIME, independently of the sleep implementation. Metadata contracts use Bash type/help builtins and the documented sleep help text.
coverage: Bash reports sleep as a builtin and exposes its documented help.
Zero and short fractional intervals, seconds suffix, and end-of-options handling.
The requested fractional delay reaches a conservative 10 ms lower bound using EPOCHREALTIME.
GNU's multiple-operand interval behavior and negative, malformed, and missing operand errors.
exclusions: Exact diagnostic wording is not asserted; error cases require nonempty stderr and the GNU exit status.
Only short durations are run. Long intervals, sub-microsecond timing precision, and scheduling accuracy beyond the 10 ms lower bound are not claimed.
Signal interruption is deferred because it needs a separately reviewed child-only signal driver and explicit proof of process isolation.

cases.purpose: Verify Bash type metadata identifies the statically enabled sleep command as a builtin.
Verify help exposes the documented minimum-delay and GNU-style interval contract.
Check that a zero-second interval succeeds immediately.
Check a fractional interval and independently confirm that at least 10 ms elapsed for a 20 ms request.
Check GNU-style seconds suffix parsing on a short interval.
Check that -- ends option parsing before a valid zero interval.
Check GNU sleep's documented behavior of summing multiple interval operands; a candidate rejection remains a compatibility failure.
Check rejection of a negative interval and GNU's failure status.
Check rejection of an unrecognized duration suffix.
Check GNU sleep's missing-operand error and status.
Qualify interrupted sleep behavior against GNU sleep.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM or reviewed mock with a child-only SIGINT driver. That fixture must prove the signal targets only the sleeping child and compare GNU and candidate status and interruption behavior; no signal injection is available in the runner contract.

cases.purpose: GNU sleep accepts an empty interval list after -- as a zero-duration sleep.
Accept multiple unit-suffixed and fractional intervals.
A malformed later operand makes the command fail.
